issues.failure_explanation: By \eqref{eq:avg_velocity_def}, $w(z;r,t)=\frac1{t-r}\int_r^t v(z_\tau,\tau)d\tau$ where $z_\tau$ is the flow trajectory through $z$ at time $t$. For two inputs $z,z'$ one gets $\|v(z_\tau,\tau)-v(z'_\tau,\tau)\|\le \mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))\|z_\tau-z'_\tau\|$, and $\|z_\tau-z'_\tau\|$ is controlled only through Grönwall by $\exp(\int_\tau^t \mathrm{Lip}(v(s,\cdot))ds)\|z-z'\|$. The theorem drops this exponential factor and asserts $\mathrm{Lip}(w)\le\frac1{t-r}\int\mathrm{Lip}(v)$, which is not a valid inference (no proof is given). The resulting constants $L_0/2$ and $1+L_0/2$ are therefore unjustified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a Grönwall argument for the flow map and replace the bound by $\frac1{t-r}\int_r^t \mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))\exp(\int_\tau^t\mathrm{Lip}(v(s,\cdot))ds)d\tau$, updating the stated constants accordingly.

issues.failure_explanation: The map $\mathcal T(\xi)=C^{1/2}\xi$ with $C$ trace-class is a bounded linear operator on $\mathcal H$ (norm $\sup_k\lambda_k^{1/2}$), hence a Lipschitz map $\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$, contradicting the Example's final claim. Moreover, when $\lambda_k k^{2s}$ is bounded (true for the paper's priors with $s\in(1/2,1]$), $C^{1/2}$ is bounded $\mathcal H^{-s}\to\mathcal H$, so a globally Lipschitz deterministic one-step transport pushing $\rho_W$ exactly to $\rho_A$ exists. Mutual singularity of $\rho_W$ and $\rho_A$ (Proposition \ref{prop:white_colored_singular}, which is correct) says nothing about existence or regularity of a transport—any pushforward between distinct measures is compatible with singularity. The only valid content is that $\rho_W$ is not supported on $\mathcal H$, so a map with domain $\mathcal H$ is undefined $\rho_W$-a.s.; this is a domain convention, not an obstruction to regular transport.
